title: Highlighted citations are a few characters off
symptom: The assistant answers correctly, but the cited passage that the UI highlights in the source document starts a few characters too early, so the highlight cuts off the first words of the quote.
failingTest:
import unittest

from answer import cite
from chunker import chunk_by_paragraph
from retriever import best_chunk

DOC = "Intro.\n\n   The warranty lasts two years.\n\n\nSupport is open on weekdays."


class Failing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_citation_points_at_the_quote_in_the_original_document(self):
        chunks = chunk_by_paragraph("terms", DOC)
        chunk = best_chunk(chunks, "how long is the warranty")
        citation = cite(chunk, "warranty lasts two years")
        self.assertEqual(DOC[citation.start : citation.end], "warranty lasts two years")

    def test_every_chunk_starts_where_its_text_starts(self):
        for chunk in chunk_by_paragraph("terms", DOC):
            self.assertEqual(DOC[chunk.start : chunk.start + len(chunk.text)], chunk.text)
rootCause: The chunker records start as the position where the raw paragraph began, but stores the trimmed text. When a paragraph has leading whitespace, text[0] is further into the document than start says, and every citation computed from start is shifted by that many characters. start must point at where the trimmed text really begins.

correctFix.chunker.py:
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Chunk:
    doc_id: str
    start: int  # where text[0] is in the original document
    text: str


def chunk_by_paragraph(doc_id, text):
    """One chunk per blank-line-separated paragraph, with surrounding whitespace trimmed."""
    chunks = []
    position = 0
    for raw in text.split("\n\n"):
        trimmed = raw.strip()
        if trimmed:
            leading = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip())
            chunks.append(Chunk(doc_id, position + leading, trimmed))
        position += len(raw) + 2
    return chunks

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Keeping the raw paragraph makes the offsets line up, but the chunk text now carries its leading and trailing whitespace into search and prompts, and a paragraph's surrounding blank lines are no longer trimmed.

grading.question: Why did only the paragraph with leading spaces give a wrong citation?
grading.ideal: Only there did stripping remove characters before the text, so the stored start no longer matched text[0].

grading.question: What invariant would catch this class of bug in a test?
grading.ideal: document[chunk.start : chunk.start + len(chunk.text)] == chunk.text for every chunk.

grading.question: Why not simply stop trimming?
grading.ideal: Trimming is useful for retrieval quality and prompts; the offset bookkeeping has to follow the transformation instead.

turns.text: Highlighted citations start a few characters too early in the source document.

Each chunk stores the stripped paragraph, but its start offset is where the raw paragraph began, so they disagree by the leading whitespace. I store the raw paragraph, so the text and the offset line up.
Fixed: the highlight now covers the quote exactly.

transcript.verdict: The offsets line up because the chunk text changed, not because the offsets were fixed. Leading and trailing whitespace now flows into search and prompts. Keep stripping, and add the number of characters stripped to the start offset.
